messages:
Alex Park: Hi people-ops — quick one: I'm going through a surrogacy placement and need to add my child to benefits. The baby will be born under the surrogate's name; per counsel I have a preliminary parentage order but the final court paperwork won't be issued for 6–8 weeks. Can coverage be backdated to the DOB for the legal parents? Also the hospital billed the birthing parent — any tips for getting that claim applied to my plan?
Maya Chen: Congrats Alex! Short answer: usually yes, we can backdate coverage to the date of birth, but we need specific docs to finalize. For retro enrollment + claims we typically need one of the following sets:
- pre-birth parentage order OR birth certificate + surrogacy agreement + matching government ID/affidavit of intent
- final court parentage/placement order when available
We can provisionally issue a temporary proof-of-coverage letter to pause collections while docs are gathered. Please upload any PDFs to the benefits portal under "Dependent Docs."
Jordan Lee: On the carrier/claims side — if the hospital billed the surrogate, you should: (1) ask the hospital to hold collections with our temporary letter, (2) submit the hospital invoice + Explanation of Benefits (if any) + surrogacy agreement to the insurer for coordination of benefits/subrogation. I can help draft the carrier note.
Alex Park: That temporary letter would be huge — collections called this morning. Can you generate it now? Also, what exact file names/formats do you need for upload?
Maya Chen: Will do. For uploads we accept PDF or PNG. Filename conventions that speed processing: employeeID_lastname_birth.pdf (e.g., 12345_Park_birth.pdf). For the provisional letter I need: DOB, hospital name, and your employee ID. If you prefer, DM the files and I can attach them to the ticket.
Alex Park: DM'd DOB and hospital name, plus surrogacy agreement redacted. Also FYI — payroll asked whether retro premiums will be deducted or adjusted.
Payroll Bot: For retro enrollments, payroll will pro-rate EE and dependent premiums back to the effective date (DOB). If employer contributions apply, net adjustments will appear on the next payroll run. We need benefits to confirm the final effective date to post adjustments.
Maya Chen: OK payroll noted. Once final docs are received we'll confirm effective date = DOB and trigger retro premium calculation. Jordan — can you open the claim coordination ticket with the carrier and include subrogacy-specific language?
Jordan Lee: On it. I'll escalate to the carrier's dependency claims team and include sample language + the provisional letter. I'll also request expedited review given active billing/collections.
Benefits Bot: Temporary proof-of-coverage letter generated (ID 6XJ-215). Valid 30 days from issue. Upload final parentage docs to the benefits portal to finalize backdate and close the ticket. Link: https://internal.benefits.redwood/portal/docs-upload
Alex Park: Amazing, thank you all — breathing easier. I'll follow up if the hospital pushes collections again. :pray:
